1 Topic Drift#

Topic-drift checks compare the principal topic words in two sets of documents. They help identify whether retrieved knowledge, generated content, or user queries have moved away from an expected topic distribution.

Section Navigation

  • 1.1 TopicSemanticContentDrift

  • 1.2 TopicContentQueryDrift

1.1 TopicSemanticContentDrift#

TopicSemanticContentDrift compares the topic distributions of reference and analysis content documents. Use it when monitoring whether new content has shifted away from an established reference corpus.

class ragscope.topic_drift.TopicSemanticContentDrift(ref_content_docs, analysis_content_docs, embedding_model)#

Bases: object

TopicSemanticContentDrift is used to assess if the topic distribution words matches between the the reference and analysis document. The main idea is to check if the new documents topics matches with the previous one based on topic distribution.

As such this uses categorical similarity methods such as braun,dice,jaccard,overlap and tanimoto coefficients.

Parameters:

  • ref_content_docs (List[str])

  • analysis_content_docs (List[str])

  • embedding_model (Any)

1.2 TopicContentQueryDrift#

TopicContentQueryDrift compares the topic distributions of knowledge-base content and user queries. Use it to assess whether queries remain aligned with the topics represented in the knowledge base.

class ragscope.topic_drift.TopicContentQueryDrift(content_docs, query_docs, embedding_model)#

Bases: object

TopicContentQueryDrift is used to assess if the topic distribution words matches between the knowledge content base and user queries. The main idea is to check if the user’s queries are within context based on the topic words distribution.

As such this uses categorical similarity methods such as braun,dice,jaccard,overlap and tanimoto coefficients.

Parameters:

  • content_docs (List[str])

  • query_docs (List[str])

  • embedding_model (Any)
